editorial.tldr: This is a loose cluster of mostly arXiv papers on agent training, alignment and knowledge handling, not one developing story. It started with RL recipes, preference-optimization variants and kernel-tuning agents, then widened to retrieval, agent memory and vision-language grounding work.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 18: NaviGATE proposes noise-aware reasoning over multimodal knowledge graphs, after a week where Jetriever ranked agent memories by usefulness instead of similarity and PhysScope targeted physics-diagram agents.
editorial.why_it_matters: If you run RAG or agent memory, these papers name concrete failure modes (models answering from pretraining instead of retrieved context, similarity search returning unhelpful memories, stale personal facts), but every result is author-reported on the papers' own benchmarks.
editorial.take_for_builders: Add eval cases where the retrieved context or image contradicts the model's prior (altered facts, decoy diagrams) and check the agent follows the evidence before adopting any new retrieval, memory or alignment recipe from this cluster.

beats.headline: RL recipes target the hard parts of training agents: delayed credit, orchestration and partial verifiers

beats.headline: Preference-optimization papers target general preferences, shifting objectives, noisy labels and missing gold answers
beats.summary: DNO empirical study, preference learning from multi-agent debate, steerable multi-objective GRPO with LoRA adapters, and PORT token reweighting.

beats.headline: Agents that tune GPU kernels and AI infrastructure get methods and benchmarks

beats.headline: Retrieval becomes an agent harness problem: context engines, compiled knowledge and graph retrieval
beats.summary: Knowledge compilation for search harnesses, InfoQ's context-engine architecture, ArcRAG, distilling lookups into weights, private retrieval, and the Thinker context-trimming tool.

beats.headline: Papers probe whether models actually use the knowledge in context and memory
beats.summary: ImplicitHop, DAMI for linear-attention recall, relational reasoning over RAG context, ROSE knowledge editing, TransMem, Knowledge Answer Divergence and Jetriever.

beats.headline: Vision-language models that hallucinate objects or reason past what they see get alignment fixes
beats.summary: MIRA, latent multimodal reasoning, VIGOR, cross-modal unlearning, VEPO, GEM-MM and severity-aware preference validation.

beats.headline: Optimization papers on routing, merchandising and federated learning ride along on shared vocabulary
beats.summary: Small-model capability routing, cold-start cover-photo selection, parallel split learning, and explainable federated learning.

beats.headline: Multimodal agents get grounding benchmarks, and knowledge-graph reasoning goes multimodal
beats.summary: Google's Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark, Vision-as-a-Tool, WebArena-Pro, ViRA, MM-ReportBench, PhysScope and NaviGATE.

open_questions: Does any independent group reproduce TSBPO's gains on long-horizon agent tasks outside the paper's own environments?
Does negative-only policy optimization train useful agents when the verifier can only reject wrong answers in real tool-use settings?
Do kernel-optimization agents beat vendor libraries and hand-tuned kernels on Infrathon or AscendGYM workloads under their cost accounting?
Does utility-based memory ranking like Jetriever beat embedding similarity on production agent memory without a large cost increase?
Do the VLM hallucination fixes (VEPO, GEM-MM, severity-aware alignment) hold up on screenshots and documents rather than natural photos?
Does external visual tooling (Vision-as-a-Tool, zooming in ViRA) beat a stronger base model's own vision on WebArena-Pro-style tasks?
